proposals: The Petroleum Ministry should define one petrochemical-intensity metric and publish it refinery by refinery every year, so that the national 13%-to-15% target, IndianOil’s 6.5%-to-16% target and the PSU composite index of 4.1 to 9.3 can be compared on a common basis.

IndianOil, BPCL and HPCL should disclose in their annual reports how each debt raise is allocated between petrochemical, refining-capacity and maintenance capex, so that a ₹15,000 crore raise can be tied to the petrochemical pivot by disclosure rather than by inference.

The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should maintain a public register of announced refinery-petrochemical projects with cost, financing structure and completion status, so that projects like Panipat, Bina, Barmer and the proposed southern and Uttar Pradesh complexes can be tracked in one official place.

The RBI should publish external commercial borrowings by refiners each quarter, with stated end-use, after the February 2026 widening of the automatic-route ceiling, so that the foreign-currency share of the petrochemical build-out is visible.
